## Elastic easing corrected

Solo Elastic easing now has a longer, more readable spring motion. The default `Out.Elastic` reaches its first overshoot around **16% of the duration instead of 12%**, and settles near **90% instead of 45%**, so the animation no longer appears to finish halfway through its allotted time.

- Retune the oscillation period and damping in both C# and GDScript, preserving the calibrated 10%–50% overshoot strengths and smooth arrival at the endpoint.
- Update the easing playground and documentation previews to match the library, with shared conformance fixtures and checks for the revised oscillation spacing.

## Documentation improvements

- Rework and polish the C# and GDScript guides throughout, with clearer explanations, corrected examples, and improved navigation in both languages.
- Add an interactive first-tween tutorial that shows how endpoints, duration, and easing change each animation. Its controls and animation state carry across language switches.
- Add a six-step anatomy walkthrough and a definitions reuse demo, showing how one definition can start multiple tweens with individual overrides. Introduce definitions before syntax sugar in the tutorial.
- Add a **Porting Godot Tweens** guide mapping Godot's transitions and easing modes to tweens.gd equivalents, including legacy easing names.
- Split custom easing into dedicated **Functions** and **Curves** guides, with redirects from the previous custom-easing pages, and improve effect previews and API explanations.

## Downloads

- **Godot addon:** `tweens.gd-0.1.4-beta.zip` includes C# and GDScript sources and prebuilt native libraries. Requires Godot 4.7.2; C# additionally requires Godot .NET and .NET 8 or later.
- **Compiled C# package:** `tweens.gd.0.1.4-beta.nupkg`, targeting .NET 8 and .NET 10, with symbols in `tweens.gd.0.1.4-beta.snupkg`.

**Full changelog:** [v0.1.3-beta…v0.1.4-beta](https://github.com/outfox/tweens.gd/compare/v0.1.3-beta...v0.1.4-beta)
